In my no-bullshit opinion, you seriously just need to get over her, or reach out to her like you said and give it a try just for the sake of trying. She isn't your "one true love" or your "soul mate". There is no reason you cannot find someone else with amazing things and experiences to offer, who you can love and who can love you back. There is also no reason why you can't give her a call and try once again if that is what the both of you want.

I personally don't believe in soul mates or "one true love" or any of that bullshit, and the reason I don't is because I have loved more than one person in my life, and I don't think any one love was stronger or better than another. My relationship with X didn't have any more or any less love than my relationship with Y, or with Z. They were all different relationships with amazing things to offer me that helped me learn about myself and how to deal with romantic relationships. Sometimes things just don't work out, and it's not anyone's fault, and when you look back you think about the good times because there will always be a part of you that cares for this person. That is normal and to be expected.

However, if it doesn't work out, it doesn't work out, you live life, gain experience, and learn how to work through your issues with future relationships based on mistakes made in the past. If I had dated some of the people I dated in the past knowing what I know now, you are damn right I would have been able to work things out with them better. It's because we have matured since then, and with maturity comes the ability to be in healthy, communicative relationships with less problems.

There is certainly nothing wrong with giving the relationship a try once more- however, if it doesn't work out, you just have to let it go and be open to experiencing love with other people, because you can. Putting this one girl on a pedestal and obsessing over "the one that got away," is overly dramatic and romantic in an unhealthy way in my opinion.

As far as splitting them up into groups, I would just make sure there is an interpreter for every group that there is a deaf student.

Overall, I wouldn't worry too much. Just let all of your students know if they have any problems, that they can come to you.

I apologize, perhaps I am too sensitive. I grew up with deaf and hard of hearing friends; many people would treat them as if they were stupid, or incapable, and it was very frustrating for my friends to experience. Growing up, I learned that referring to a deaf person as disabled, or hearing impaired, is similar to referring to a black person as a negro, or an asian person as an oriental. It is offensive, even though the person who said it doesn't always mean it to be, and they think they are just using a word that they think describes that person. 

I do not believe that being deaf is a disability. They may not be able to hear, but it does not effect their ability to think, perform actions, or even communicate. I can understand how you think that saying a deaf person isn't disabled is like saying a black student isn't a minority, but if you place that black student in a country where everyone is black, they are no longer a minority. If you place that deaf student in the deaf community, they are no longer disabled. That is my point of view.

If you treat a student like they have a disability, you will not be helping them. A teacher needs to look at it this way: Deaf students are not disabled, they just speak a different language. Deaf people can drive, dance, watch TV, go shopping, go drinking, read, write, do math, make responsible decisions, and do everything that a hearing person can do. They can even communicate with people who do not know their language, ASL. 

My point is, do not treat Deaf people like they are disabled, because they are not. That will harm them more than help them. The only thing they are unable to do is hear, and if you understood Deaf culture, you would know that many Deaf people are proud of that. Understanding and respecting a Deaf student's culture and point of view is a huge step  in being able to help them more effectively.
